newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Shipowners seek risk management to buy bunker fuel.
newsitem.headline: Shipowners seek risk management to buy bunker fuel.

text.p: The huge cost to shippers of fuel is prompting them to increasingly consider hedging their financial risk, in what can be a volatile market, a senior shipping official said on Thursday.

"Bunker planning which involves when, where and how much to buy could save a company 25-30 percent savings in terms of overall energy costs," said S.S Rangnekar, director of the Shipping Corporation of India.
He was speaking at the two-day International Bunkering Conference in Singapore.
Rangnekar said global bunker consumption is about 140 to 150 million tonnes per year, which costs shipping companies about US$23 billion.
"The bunker fuels which account for about 30-40 percent of shipowner's operating costs and is the single most important costs element in shipping operations," he told the conference.
Financial brokers, such as in Singapore, are increasingly offering hedge instruments specifically geared to the bunker market.
Rangnekar said shipper can face unreliable bunker suppliers, or poor bunker fuel, which in the long run costs the industry more.
He suggested that shipowners should spend more time planning bunker purchases, looking into prices, port costs and infrastructure, and if necessary extra time in port.
On quality, he said "the best thing under the existing circumstances is to choose reliable and reputed quality bunker suppliers port wise than to deal with all and sundry."
